title: onboarding writes an external project's private design.md under FM_HOME only (never in the repository, guarded at publication), as firstmate's own reference that records the base commit it describes; every fm project sync tells firstmate when the base has moved past it, with the commits and files, and fm-project.sh design-checked re-binds it; an existing design.md is never overwritten
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-05 the first external dispatch for the pilot external project (example-org/example-repo) failed to pin with `missing approved source: <external project path>`; firstmate hand-wrote the file. Spec v1 (PR #211, head e8c6d66) seeded the file on onboarding with an empty captain-fill 'task intents' section. On merge card D-firstmate-workflow-T226-2 the captain rejected that (2026-10-06): 'design.md不一定放在外部repo根目錄, 也不應該進外部目錄版本控制, 純屬firstmate內部流程參考, 可能隨著其他人commit, 合併PR等等動作讓design.md過時, 這時候要能發現更正'. v2 therefore: (1) the file lives only under FM_HOME/projects/<name>/ and is guarded out of the external repository; (2) it is firstmate's own reference, with no section for the captain to fill; (3) it records the external base commit it describes; (4) firstmate is told when the base has moved past that commit, with the commits and files, so it can review and correct the file. Detection never blocks a dispatch and never edits the design content.

Mechanism (root cause, unchanged from v1). `bin/fm-project.sh add` execs `bin/fm-onboard.sh` (fm-project.sh:34-36), which runs `bin/lib/fm_onboard.py main`; on confirmed answers it calls `approve(home, e, p, answers)` (fm_onboard.py:427). `approve()` (fm_onboard.py:249-283) writes `state/onboarding/inspection.json`, `state/config.yaml` and `CONVENTIONS.md` (:280-282) and nothing else. The external design source is `FM_HOME/projects/<name>/design.md`: `fm_registry.py:509` resolves the `design` field of an external entry to `<home>/design.md` (`fm_project_get <name> design` prints it; fm-config.sh:983 exports it as FM_DESIGN), and `fm_autopilot.py:292-293` uses the same path. The pin reads it in `SpecPins.snapshot` (bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py:146-172): for an external project a missing file raises `missing approved source` (:163) because `collect()` (:174-180) does not pass `optional` for design. The private design path `<home>/design.md` is a sibling of the managed clone `<home>/repo` (fm-project.sh:101-102), never inside it. `fm-project.sh sync` (bin/fm-project.sh:133-177, `sync_clone`) is the one place that fetches an external base: it is run by `fm_external_prepare` (bin/fm-config.sh:1007-1013) before every external worker round (bin/fm-worker.sh:81), review and spec preflight (bin/fm-review.sh:83), and by hand. The owned conventions watcher re-inspects each project every `reinspect_seconds` in a child process (bin/lib/fm_conventions_watch.py:54-73, the `__main__` block :92-96) but fetches nothing today.

Change 1 — seed (bin/lib/fm_onboard.py). In `approve()`, right after `atomic(home/'CONVENTIONS.md', render(p))` (:282), write `home/'design.md'` with the existing `atomic()` helper (fm_onboard.py:25-37: parent 0700, file 0600, refuses a symlink) when, and only when, nothing exists at that path. If `home/'design.md'` is a symlink (dangling or not) raise ValueError('refusing symlink: …'); if it exists as a regular file leave it byte-for-byte unchanged. Add `design_seed(name, p, contract)` returning the text. `name` is `home.name`; `contract` is `answers['contract']`. Template (exact; `{x}` is the value, lists joined with ', ', booleans as Python `str()`): `---`; `based_on: unrecorded`; `checked_at: unrecorded`; `---`; `# {name}: private design`; blank; `Firstmate's private reference for this project, written by fm project add at {p[confirmed_at]}. It lives only under FM_HOME, never in the repository. based_on is the {p[base]} commit it was last checked against; when {p[base]} moves past it, fm project sync reports the commits and files so firstmate can correct this file and run fm-project.sh design-checked {name}. Onboarding never rewrites it.`; blank; `## 1. Product intent`; blank; `{p[product]}`; blank; `Captain intent ({p[confirmed_at]}): {p[captain]} — {p[intent]}`; blank; `## 2. Repository and checks`; blank; `- Repository: {p[repository]}, base {p[base]}`; `- Check: {contract[check]}`; `- Setup: {contract[setup]}` (only when the contract has a non-empty `setup`); `- Required checks: {required_checks joined}`; blank; `## 3. Policy`; blank; `- Land: {p[land]}; review: {p[review]}; post: {p[post]}`; `- Merge method: {p[merge_method]}; delete branch: {p[delete_branch]}`; the file ends with one newline. There is NO task-intents section and nothing addressed to the captain. Values come only from the validated policy `p` and the answers' contract. `edit()` and `drift()` never touch design.md.

Change 2 — the check (new bin/lib/fm_design_check.py, stdlib only, `sys.dont_write_bytecode = True`). Front matter: the file is read as text; if it starts with a line `---` and has a later line `---`, the lines between are `key: value`; only `based_on` and `checked_at` are read. A missing front matter, a missing key or a value that is not 40 hex characters means unrecorded. Command `check --engine E --name N --home H --base B`: if H/design.md is absent, print nothing and exit 0; if it is a symlink, print `fm-project: refusing symlink design.md of N` to stderr and exit 0 without reading it (this branch matters only for direct calls of the module: through fm-project.sh, `fm_project_get <name> home` already refuses a symlinked design.md in bin/lib/fm_project_paths.py:40-43, so sync, design-checked and the watcher's registry read exit 65 with that refusal before the check runs); read `origin = git -C H/repo rev-parse --verify refs/remotes/origin/B^{commit}` (missing clone or ref: print nothing, exit 0). Status: `fresh` when based_on == origin (print nothing); `unrecorded` (print one stderr line `fm-project: design.md of N is not bound to a B commit; review it against <origin12> and run fm-project.sh design-checked N`); `stale` otherwise. For stale: if `git cat-file -e <based_on>^{commit}` fails, the report says `based_on <based12> is not in the clone's history (rewritten?)` with no lists; else `commits` = `git log --format='%h %s' -n 20 <based_on>..<origin>` and `files` = `git diff --name-only <based_on> <origin>` (keep the first 50 and the total count). Print one stderr line `fm-project: design.md of N may be stale: B moved <based12>..<origin12> (<c> commits, <f> files); review it and run fm-project.sh design-checked N`. Every git call uses `-C H/repo`, a 30 s timeout, stdin DEVNULL, and is treated as unreadable (status unknown, print nothing, exit 0) on any failure. Record `{status, based_on, origin, commits, files, files_total, at}` in H/state/onboarding/design-check.json with `fm_onboard.save`. Wake: only for `stale`, and only when the pair (based_on, origin) differs from the pair stored as `notified` in that JSON: call `fm_lifeline.forward(E, N, 'design-stale', 'design_stale', <the stderr line without its `fm-project: ` prefix>)` (bin/lib/fm_lifeline.py:568-593, added by T-224) and then store `notified`. `forward()` appends straight to E/state/session/wake.jsonl and rings only E/state/session/wake.d, whatever FM_PROJECT, FM_EXTERNAL or `default_project` say, so the wake always reaches firstmate and is never doubled by `push()`'s own forwarding; the commits and files stay in design-check.json, not on the queue item. `design_stale` is a wake reason, not an fm-emit event type, so bin/fm-emit.sh and bin/fm-diagram.sh's ROUTINE list do not change. The check always exits 0; it never edits design.md. Command `mark --engine E --name N --home H --base B` (Change 3) is in the same module.

Change 3 — wiring (bin/fm-project.sh). (a) In `sync_clone`, after the clone is configured and before the final `exit 0` (:177), run `python3 "$_fm_code_dir/lib/fm_design_check.py" check --engine "$REPO" --name "$NAME" --home "$project_home" --base "$base" || true`. Sync's exit status and its existing stdout lines do not change. (b) New subcommand `design-checked <name> [--repo dir]`: add it to the usage line (:71) and the accepted commands (:87); self (`repo: .`) prints the existing 'nothing to' line and exits 0; it requires `place_ok` and `is_clone` (exit 65 with a reason otherwise) and runs `python3 "$_fm_code_dir/lib/fm_design_check.py" mark ...`. `mark` refuses (exit 65, reason on stderr) a missing or symlinked design.md or a missing `refs/remotes/origin/B`; otherwise it sets based_on to that origin commit and checked_at to the current UTC time (ISO 8601, `Z`), replacing the two keys inside an existing front matter or prepending the four-line front matter when there is none, leaves every other byte of the file unchanged, writes with `fm_onboard.atomic` (0600, symlink refusal), records status `fresh` in design-check.json, prints `fm-project: design.md of N checked against B <origin12>` and pushes no wake. It does not fetch: firstmate runs sync first. (c) Re-inspect cadence: in bin/lib/fm_conventions_watch.py add `design_sync(engine, name, run=subprocess.run)` that runs `[<code dir>/fm-project.sh, 'sync', name, '--repo', str(engine)]` with stdin DEVNULL and a 300 s timeout, and returns its exit code (a timeout or OSError returns 70 and is written to H/state/onboarding/inspection-error.txt via `atomic`); call it from the `__main__` block after `inspect_and_propose(...)`. The inline (owner=None) path used by tests and `tick()`'s scheduling do not change. A watcher sync can collide on a git ref lock with a round's own `fm_external_prepare` fetch, which then exits 65 for that round exactly as two parallel rounds can today; with the default daily `reinspect_seconds` (fm_onboard.py:174) this is rare, and the design check itself never fails a sync or a dispatch.

Change 4 — publication guard (bin/fm-config.sh `fm_private_stage`, :1125-1131, and bin/lib/fm_config_runtime.py `private_stage`, :69-75). `fm_private_stage` passes its tree: `... | python3 "$_fm_code_dir/lib/fm_config_runtime.py" private-stage "$1"`. `private_stage()` keeps the `.fm-*` refusal unchanged and, when `sys.argv[1]` (the tree) is given and the environment's FM_DESIGN names a regular file (an external round's storage init exports it, bin/fm-config.sh:983-989), reads that file's bytes and, for each staged path, the index blob `git -C <tree> cat-file blob :<path>` (30 s timeout; any failure counts as no match); any staged blob byte-identical to the private design refuses with exit 65 and `fm: the private design.md cannot be committed: [paths]`. Callers: bin/fm-worker.sh:2074 and bin/fm-checkpoint.sh:126 call `fm_private_stage "$tree"` already; tests/external-execution.test.sh:185-191 stubs `git` as a shell function for the diff and sets no FM_DESIGN, so its case is unchanged; :277 replaces fm_private_stage with a no-op and is unchanged.

Migration. Existing private design files have no front matter, so the first sync after merge prints the unrecorded line and pushes no wake; firstmate (SKILL.md step below) reviews the pilot external project's design.md against master and runs `fm-project.sh design-checked the pilot external project` once. Pins are unaffected: an external pin snapshots design.md as text (fm_spec_pins.py:155-163) and verifies only the frozen snapshot's hash (:303-311), so `mark` and firstmate's edits never break an in-flight pin; the next pin snapshots the new bytes. Pin acceptance needs no code change (any regular file at the external design path), and `fm_project_paths.py:40` still refuses a symlinked design.md.

Tests (fail-first; workers do not run suites; CI and the gates verify). (a) tests/onboard-cli.test.sh, after the existing successful `add ... --answers` (the `seed` project): `$FM_HOME/projects/seed/design.md` exists with mode 600 (read with `python3 -c 'import os,sys;print(oct(os.stat(sys.argv[1]).st_mode&0o777))'`, expect `0o600`), starts with `---`, contains `based_on: unrecorded`, `# seed: private design`, `Private product brief`, `- Check: npm test`, `- Setup: npm ci`, `- Repository: owner/product, base main`, and lacks `Task intents`; `fm_project_get seed design` prints that path (the file's idiom, :26); and `test ! -e $FM_HOME/projects/seed/repo/design.md`. The unconfirmed-proposal assertion gains `test ! -e $FM_HOME/projects/seed/design.md`. (b) tests/onboarding.test.sh `test_confirmation_write_edit_drift` (around :88-105): after the first approve(), the file equals `design_seed(home.name, p, self.answers()['contract'])`; write `firstmate edit\n`, call approve() again, the file still reads `firstmate edit\n`; the import line (:24) gains `design_seed`. (c) Same file: `home/'design.md'` a symlink to a temp file before approve() raises ValueError and leaves the target unchanged. (d) New tests/design-check.test.sh, built like tests/project.test.sh:1-45 (unset FM_*/HERDR_*, safe_tmpdir, engine with .githooks and a two-project config, a bare 'GitHub' repo under FM_GITHUB_URL, FM_GH=tests/gh-stub.sh, a real seed repo; no network): after `sync` with a design.md that has no front matter, stderr contains `is not bound to a` and the engine's state/session/wake.jsonl has no `design_stale` item; `design-checked` exits 0, the file now starts with the front matter whose based_on equals the bare repo's trunk sha and the original body bytes follow unchanged, mode stays 0o600; a second `sync` prints nothing about design.md; a new commit touching `src/a.txt` pushed to the bare repo, then `sync`: exit 0, stderr contains `may be stale` and `1 commits, 1 files`, design-check.json has status stale and files [`src/a.txt`], and the engine's wake queue has exactly one item with `reason` `forwarded` and `origin_reason` `design_stale` whose line names the project; repeat that stale case in a second engine whose config sets `default_project:` to the external project and with `FM_PROJECT=example-app FM_EXTERNAL=1` exported, and the item still lands in that engine's own state/session/wake.jsonl and nothing is written to the project's private queue; a third `sync` with no new commit adds no second wake; `design-checked` again, then `sync` prints nothing; a symlinked design.md makes sync exit 65 with the registry's `symlink` refusal (bin/lib/fm_project_paths.py:40-43), and `python3 bin/lib/fm_design_check.py check` called directly on that home prints `refusing symlink` and exits 0; `design-checked` on a missing design.md exits 65; a based_on that is not in the history reports `not in the clone's history`. The case runs the real `bin/fm-project.sh` by path. (e) tests/external-execution.test.sh: a new case with a real temp git repo (FM_EXTERNAL=1, FM_DESIGN pointing at a temp file) in which a staged file byte-identical to the design refuses with exit 65 and names the path, and a staged different file passes. (f) tests/conventions-watch.test.sh: `C.design_sync(engine, 'one', run=<recording stub>)` calls `fm-project.sh sync one --repo <engine>` with a positive timeout and stdin DEVNULL; a stub raising subprocess.TimeoutExpired returns 70 and writes inspection-error.txt. (a)-(f) fail on base. No helper in tests/*.sh may be named `assert_*` unless tests/lib.sh defines it (bin/ci.sh:1134-1153), and every variable directly before non-ASCII text in new bilingual strings is braced.

Callers, mirrors and fixtures checked: `grep -rn 'approve(' bin tests` lists bin/lib/fm_onboard.py:427 (the add path), bin/fm-canary.sh:673 (external destroy fixture), tests/onboarding.test.sh:79, :81, :86, :91, :109, :110, :125, :146 and :159, tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh:25, tests/conventions-watch.test.sh:35, tests/conventions-publication.test.sh:77, tests/project.test.sh:216, tests/external-review-launchers.test.sh:21, tests/external-review-entrypoint.test.sh:26, tests/external-reviews.test.sh:261, tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py:593, tests/lib/external_entrypoints.py:74 (its `policy()` calls approve() again with other `delete` values: the first call creates design.md and later calls leave it alone; nothing there reads design.md) and tests/lib/external_stock.py:81 (approve) with :88 (it then writes its own `design.md` sentinel with `write_text`, which still overwrites as before). Each passes a temp home; the new file appears there and nothing asserts its absence or the `missing approved source` text. No caller writes design.md before approve() expecting it to be replaced. tests/dispatch.test.sh:86 defines an unrelated shell `approve`. None needs a change for v2's seed either; the PR says so for each. tests/onboarding.test.sh's import line (:24) gains `design_seed`. Two suites reach approve() through `fm-project.sh add` rather than a direct call: tests/onboard-register.test.sh via `add_seed` (:34-35, called at :45, :56, :70, :80, :97, :105, :113, :156; it re-onboards the same home, so it relies on the 'existing design.md is left alone' rule) and tests/onboard-remote.test.sh:36 (one successful add; the refusals at :43 and :47 stop before approve(), fm_onboard.py:420-426). Neither asserts the home's contents, so neither changes. bin/lib/fm_conventions_watch.py:13 imports from fm_onboard but not approve(); it changes only by Change 3(c). Suites that reach `fm-project.sh sync` (directly or through `fm_external_prepare`): tests/project.test.sh (its homes get a seeded design.md only after :216; the later syncs at :316, :345 assert exit codes, and the stderr assertions at :325-:405 are `assert_contains` on refusal text, so the extra unrecorded line does not change them), tests/project-worktrees.test.sh, tests/onboard-remote.test.sh, tests/external-execution.test.sh, tests/spec-pin-sync.test.sh, tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh, tests/guard.test.sh, tests/project-migration.test.sh and tests/external-stock-dispatch.test.sh (tests/lib/external_stock.py:88 overwrites design.md with a sentinel that has no front matter: unrecorded, no wake). The worker greps each for an assertion that sync's stderr is empty or that the engine wake queue has an exact count, and adjusts only a fixture that would change, saying so in the PR; an unrecorded file never pushes a wake, so wake counts change only where a fixture records a based_on.

Design and skill (edit in place, no new section at the end, T-189). design/design.md §15.2, subsection '#### T-139 private onboarding contract': after the sentence ending `with explicit captain-confirmed checks, policy, product intent and commands.` (design.md:4870) add: `The same confirmation writes an initial private design.md beside it (T-226): firstmate's own reference for the project, seeded from the confirmed product intent, captain intent, checks and policy, stored only under FM_HOME and refused by the publication guard if a round stages its bytes. Its front matter records based_on, the base commit it was last checked against. Every fm project sync (and so every external round, review and preflight, and the watcher's re-inspection) compares based_on with origin/<base>; when the base moved, it prints the commits and changed files, records them in state/onboarding/design-check.json and pushes one design_stale wake per new base, so firstmate reviews and corrects the file and runs fm-project.sh design-checked <name>. The check never blocks a dispatch and never edits the file; onboarding never overwrites an existing design.md.` skills/firstmate/SKILL.md, section '## Repository onboarding (T-139)' (:1001-1045): after the paragraph about the owned watcher (ending `cannot grant permission.`), add one paragraph: after onboarding (and once for a project whose design.md predates T-226), run `bin/fm-project.sh sync <name>`, review the private design.md against the base, edit it in place, then run `bin/fm-project.sh design-checked <name> --repo <engine>`; on a `design_stale` wake, read the listed commits and files, correct the file, and run design-checked again; never commit design.md into the project's repository.

Out of scope: the content firstmate writes into design.md beyond the seed; `fm project edit`/`drift`; the self project (`repo: .`, design/design.md); the pin code and registry; CONVENTIONS.md rendering; autopilot handling of the new wake reason (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:704-713 ignores reasons it does not know, which is intended); T-224's forwarding. Do not touch ~/.firstmate or any real FM_HOME.
